A '''syntractrix''' is a [[curve]] of the form 

:<math>x+\sqrt{b^2-y^2}= a \ln \frac{b+\sqrt{b^2-y^2}}{y}.</math><ref>George Salmon (1879). ''A Treatise on the Higher Plane Curves: Intended as a Sequel to A Treatise on Conic Sections''. Published by Hodges, Foster, and Figgis. Page 290. [https://books.google.com/books?id=Vv43AAAAMAAJ&pg=PA289]</ref>
[[File:Syntractrix a=0.5 b=1.png|center|thumb|350px|The syntractrix for <math>a=0.5</math> and <math>b=1.</math>]]
[[File:Syntractrix a=1.5 b=1.png|center|thumb|350px|The syntractrix for <math>a=1.5</math> and <math>b=1.</math>]]

It is the locus of a point on the tangent of a [[tractrix]] at a constant distance from the point of tangency, as the point of tangency is moved along the curve.<ref>[[Dionysius Lardner]], ''A system of algebraic geometry'' 1823, p. 261–263 [https://books.google.com/books?id=0zUDAAAAQAAJ&q=Syntractrix]</ref>
